value_stream.name: Cross-Channel Fraud Management & Payment Fraud Protection

fields.Participants: Fraud Investigators, Legal (links to VS-100), LP (links to VS-23), Channels (links to VS-07/VS-10/VS-80/VS-13), Privacy (links to VS-91), HR for employee cases (links to VS-19)
fields.Trigger: Confirmed-fraud case (links to W3860); escalated alert

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Investigators conduct structured investigation per typology" (replaces manual Step 1).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: chain-of-custody discipline and Legal review; operational: closed-loop feedback to W3862
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence-admissibility risk**: Evidence not preserved to a legal/hireable standard; mitigated by chain-of-custody discipline and Legal review
- **Learning-loss risk**: Case outcomes not fed back to detection; mitigated by closed-loop feedback to W3862
System Touchpoints: - Case management; POS journal (links to VS-08); CCTV (links to VS-23); digital forensics (links to VS-27.3); ecommerce (links to VS-10); legal matters (links to VS-100); HR case (links to VS-19); insurance (links to VS-26)

steps.activity: Investigators conduct structured investigation per typology (links to W3858): transaction reconstruction, CCTV/POS-journal correlation (links to VS-08/VS-23), digital forensics for ATO/ecommerce (links to VS-10/VS-27.3), interview of staff/customers, and structured evidence pack with chain-of-custody

Investigators adjudicate against the evidence standard (confirmed / probable / dismissed), determine loss quantum and recovery potential (links to W3874), and decide referral path (recovery, law-enforcement links to W3877, employment action links to W3876, insurance links to VS-26)
Fraud Management close cases with root-cause, control-gap identification, and learning fed back to rules/models/policy (links to W3862) and to the typology catalog (links to W3858)

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, Finance/AR (links to VS-16/VS-17), Legal (links to VS-100), Collections (links to VS-16), LP (links to VS-23), Treasury (links to VS-18), Insurance (links to VS-26)
fields.Volume: Recovery target ~20–50% of confirmed fraud loss

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Fraud Management/Finance quantify recoverable loss" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with law-enforcement asset recovery" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record recoveries against the original loss" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: account-offset and prioritized civil action; operational: subrogation coordination (links to VS-26)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-recovery risk**: Customer-side fraud losses hard to recover at PH scale; mitigated by account-offset and prioritized civil action
- **Double-recovery risk**: Same loss recovered from insurance and customer; mitigated by subrogation coordination (links to VS-26)
System Touchpoints: - AR/collections (links to VS-16); GL (links to VS-17); loyalty/gift balance offset (links to VS-13/VS-54); legal matters (links to VS-100); insurance claims (links to VS-26); treasury (links to VS-18)
Time Estimate: - ~1–6 hrs/case recovery effort; recovery cycle 30–180 days

steps.activity: Fraud Management/Finance quantify recoverable loss (principal + cost), identify recovery sources (customer account balance/points/gift balance offset links to VS-13/VS-54, restitution agreement, civil/criminal recovery links to VS-100, insurance claim links to VS-26, vendor/3P recovery), and prioritize by quantum

Fraud Management/Legal/Collections pursue recovery: demand letters, restitution agreements, account-offset, small-claims/civil action where material, and coordinate with law-enforcement asset recovery (links to W3877)

Fraud Management/Finance/Treasury record recoveries against the original loss (links to VS-17 GL), report net loss-rate (links to W3880), and recover via insurance where applicable (links to VS-26/W26.3)

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, Payments (links to VS-80), Ecommerce (links to VS-10), Logistics (links to VS-06/VS-56), Legal (links to VS-100), Finance (links to VS-17), CX (links to VS-13), Insights (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Chargeback received (links to W3870); dispute cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-route of "route service-disputes to CX/quality" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "assemble and submit representment within scheme SLA" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track representment outcomes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: SLA tracker and pre-assembled evidence templates; operational: analytics (links to VS-118)
Pain Points / Risks: - **SLA-miss risk**: Late representment auto-loses the dispute; mitigated by SLA tracker and pre-assembled evidence templates
- **Fee-leakage risk**: Chargeback fees and pre-arb costs erode recovery; mitigated by analytics (links to VS-118)
System Touchpoints: - Chargeback/acquirer platform (links to VS-80); ecommerce (links to VS-10); delivery POD (links to VS-06.3/VS-56); CX/quality (links to VS-13/VS-31); identity (links to VS-126); revenue assurance (links to VS-118); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/Payments triage chargebacks by reason code (fraud vs service/quality vs authorization), decide contest-vs-accept, and route service-disputes to CX/quality (links to VS-13/VS-31) and fraud-disputes to representment

Fraud Management/Logistics assemble and submit representment within scheme SLA (Visa/Mastercard/QRPh): order details, delivery POD/photo/signature (links to VS-06.3), IP/device match, auth/AVS results, customer comms, prior history

Fraud Management/Insights track representment outcomes (win-rate, pre-arb, fee leakage links to VS-118), identify serial chargeback customers (links to VS-126), and feed learnings to ecommerce scoring (links to W3866) and acquirer relationships (links to VS-80)

fields.Owner: Fraud Management / LP / HR / Internal Audit
fields.Participants: Fraud Management, LP (links to VS-23), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), Legal (links to VS-100), IT Security (links to VS-27.3), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Speak-Up (links to VS-119)
fields.Trigger: Employee-fraud alert (links to W3865/W3860); tip-off (links to VS-119)

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Audit investigate employee fraud" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with speak-up confidentiality" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Fraud Management/Internal-Audit report material employee fraud to the Audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: HR/Legal due-process; operational: speak-up protection (links to VS-119)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Due-process risk**: Mishandled investigation creates NLRC/bogus-termination exposure (links to VS-84); mitigated by HR/Legal due-process
- **Retaliation risk**: Whistleblower on employee fraud suffers retaliation; mitigated by speak-up protection (links to VS-119)
System Touchpoints: - LP/CCTV (links to VS-23); POS journal (links to VS-08); expense/P-card (links to VS-34.3); procurement/AP (links to VS-15); IT access logs (links to VS-27.3); HR case (links to VS-19/VS-103); audit (links to VS-21); speak-up (links to VS-119)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/LP/Internal-Audit investigate employee fraud: cashier theft/sweethearting (links to W3865), refund/void manipulation, expense/P-card fraud (links to VS-34.3), procurement kickback/vendor collusion (links to VS-15/VS-86.3), data/credential misuse (links to VS-27.3), and vendor-side collusion with buyers

Fraud Management/HR/Legal handle employment-aspect: due-process (NLRC/DOLE — links to VS-84), administrative investigation, evidence preservation, suspension/termination decision, and restitution/recovery (links to W3874); coordinate with speak-up confidentiality (links to VS-119) and retaliation protection

Fraud Management/Internal-Audit report material employee fraud to the Audit Committee (links to VS-21/VS-36), refer for prosecution where material (links to W3877), and close control gaps (segregation of duties links to W1408, access reviews links to VS-27)

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance (links to VS-22), Privacy/DPO (links to VS-91), AML (links to VS-86), Finance (links to VS-17), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Corporate Affairs (links to VS-14.3/VS-104)
fields.Trigger: Material fraud event; mandatory report; law-enforcement referral

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Fraud Management/Legal/Compliance assess reportability" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track cases through prosecution" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: triage protocol and DPO coordination; operational: coordinated comms (links to VS-14)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-disclosure risk**: Missed NPC 72-hour or AMLC STR window creates regulatory liability; mitigated by triage protocol and DPO coordination
- **Reputational risk**: Public fraud event damages trust; mitigated by coordinated comms (links to VS-14.3)
System Touchpoints: - Legal matters (links to VS-100); AML/STR (links to VS-86); privacy/breach (links to VS-91); insurance (links to VS-26); audit committee (links to VS-21/VS-36); corp comms (links to VS-14.3)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/Legal/Compliance assess reportability: AML/STR to AMLC where predicate offense (links to VS-86), data-breach to NPC under RA 10173 if applicable (links to VS-91), insurance notice (links to VS-26), audit committee disclosure (links to VS-21/VS-36), and securities/board disclosure for material loss

Fraud Management/Legal coordinate law-enforcement referral (PNP-CIDG/NBI/Cybercrime for organized/ecommerce/ATO), provide evidence packs (links to W3873), and track cases through prosecution (links to VS-100 matter management)

Fraud Management/Corporate-Affairs manage external communications on material/visible fraud events (links to VS-14.3) and protect brand/reputation (links to VS-100/W1562), with privacy-by-design in any disclosure

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Risk (links to VS-21), External Audit (links to VS-17), Compliance (links to VS-22), IT Security (links to VS-27.3), Payments (links to VS-80)
fields.Trigger: Audit plan (links to VS-21); controls cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Fraud Management/Internal-Audit maintain the fraud-control register mapped to typologies" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "testing of key controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report control effectiveness to the Audit Committee" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: register tied to typology catalog; operational: CSA cadence and remediation tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Control-gap risk**: Typology without a mapped control; mitigated by register tied to typology catalog
- **Audit-finding risk**: Key controls fail testing; mitigated by CSA cadence and remediation tracking
System Touchpoints: - Controls register (links to internal-controls-matrix); audit (links to VS-21); access/SoD (links to VS-27 W1408); PCI-DSS (links to VS-27.3 W1205); payments (links to VS-80); audit committee (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/Internal-Audit maintain the fraud-control register mapped to typologies (links to W3858) and internal controls (links to internal-controls-matrix), with control owners, frequency, and evidence

Fraud Management run quarterly control self-assessment (CSA links to VS-27 W387) and Internal Audit performs periodic testing of key controls (refund authorization, override thresholds, scoring effectiveness, segregation of duties links to W1408)
Fraud Management support external audit and acquirer/PCI assessments (links to VS-27.3 W1205), remediate findings, and report control effectiveness to the Audit Committee (links to VS-21/VS-36)
steps.r: Fraud Management / Internal Audit / IT Security

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, L&D (links to VS-19.4/VS-124), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Ecommerce (links to VS-10), Customer Service (links to VS-13/VS-32), HR (links to VS-19), Sales Enablement (links to VS-124)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-alert of "Fraud Management/Store-Ops deliver training via LMS" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-measure of "measure awareness effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: role-specific training; operational: onboarding integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Awareness-gap risk**: Frontline unaware of refund/override fraud schemes; mitigated by role-specific training
- **Turnover risk**: 15–20% turnover erodes trained-base; mitigated by onboarding integration
System Touchpoints: - L&D/LMS (links to VS-19.4); store comms (links to VS-63); enablement (links to VS-124); insights (links to VS-28.1); LP (links to VS-23)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/L&D develop role-specific fraud-awareness training: cashiers (override/refund/returns fraud), customer-service (return/refund abuse), ecommerce ops (chargeback/ATO), trade sales (application/BEC), buyers (procurement fraud links to VS-86.3), and managers (investigation escalation)

Fraud Management/Store-Ops deliver training via LMS (links to VS-19.4), micro-learning and huddle alerts (links to VS-63 store comms / VS-124 enablement), and brief on emerging schemes (links to W3858)
Fraud Management measure awareness effectiveness (incident-rate by store, training completion, mystery-shop on refund/override compliance) and reinforce high-risk stores (links to VS-23/W3850)

fields.Participants: Fraud Management, Insights (links to VS-28.1), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Risk/Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Channels (links to VS-07/VS-10/VS-80/VS-13), Strategy (links to VS-33), Data Science (links to VS-30.2)
fields.Volume: Enterprise fraud scorecard (~10–15 KPIs by channel)

workflows.name: Fraud Analytics, Loss Rates & Program KPI Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Fraud Management/Insights produce the monthly fraud scorecard" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "enterprise fraud-loss rate vs appetite" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-allocate of "reallocate controls/spend to highest-loss channels, prioritize detection backlog" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-606 (ensure controlled execution — Investigation, Recovery, Compliance & Analytics (PA-125.3).)
- operational: reconciled taxonomy; operational: near-real-time loss dashboards
Pain Points / Risks: - **Double-count risk**: Same loss in shrink, leakage, and fraud; mitigated by reconciled taxonomy
- **Decision-latency risk**: Loss data arrives too late to act; mitigated by near-real-time loss dashboards
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-28.1); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); LP shrink (links to VS-23); revenue assurance (links to VS-118); audit committee (links to VS-21/VS-36); strategy (links to VS-33); model governance (links to W3862)

steps.activity: Fraud Management/Insights produce the monthly fraud scorecard: gross/net loss by channel and typology, loss-rate (% of revenue/transactions), chargeback rate, recovery rate, false-positive rate, case SLA, model performance — reconciled to shrink (links to VS-23) and revenue assurance (links to VS-118) to avoid double-count

Fraud Management/Finance/Risk roll up to the enterprise fraud-loss rate vs appetite (links to W3857), quantify financial impact on EBITDA (links to VS-17.4), and brief the Audit & Risk Committee (links to VS-21/VS-36)
Fraud Management/Strategy use analytics to reallocate controls/spend to highest-loss channels, prioritize detection backlog (links to W3859), and drive continuous improvement of the program
